newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa minister, business to meet on labour bill.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa minister, business to meet on labour bill.

text.p: Labour Minister Tito Mboweni would meet business representatives later on Thursday to discuss controversial labour legislation which sparked a one-day national strike this week, the labour ministry said.
"Today's meeting follows a request from Business South Africa (BSA) last week that Mr Mboweni meet with them to discuss the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill," the ministry said in a statement.
Among the BSA members expected to attend the meeting in Cape Town at 3.15 p.m. (1315 GMT) were Leslie Boyd, Adrian du Plessis, Bobby Godsell and Raymond Parsons.
A representative from the National African Federated Chamber of Commerce was also expected to attend the talks.
The 1.9-million member Congress of South African Trade Unions held a one-day national strike on Monday to protest against several provisions in the draft employment law.
The bill, approved by the cabinet in April, provides for a 45-hour working week and four months of maternity leave.
Cosatu wants a 40-hour week phased in within five years, six months of maternity leave and the minimum age for formal employment to be set at 18.
It is also opposed to the right of employers to apply for variations of, or exemptions from, the minimum standards set out in the bill.

Business strongly disagrees with proposals for a reduction in the working week to 40 hours, a reduction in the overtime rate from time-and-a-third to time-and-a-half and provisions for three days' paid "family responsibility" leave.
